newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria clears way for Albania security mission.
newsitem.headline: Austria clears way for Albania security mission.

text.p: Austria's parliament voted on Thursday to allow Austrian troops to take part in peacekeeping missions abroad, clearing the way for them to join an international security force for Albania.

The Austrian news agency APA reported that the new law had been agreed with the votes of the ruling coalition of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party as well as the support of the opposition Liberals.
Austria plans to send some 120 troops to violence-stricken Albania next week as part of an Italian-led mission to the anarchic Balkan state.

Austrian law formerly restricted the country's troops to participating abroad only in U.N.-led missions. A total of some 40,000 Austrian soldiers have been stationed abroad on such missions since 1960.

The new law enables Austria to contribute troops to missions led by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) or similar operations within the framework of NATO's Partnership for Peace initiative.
